reason: E1 confirms that melt-spinning yields an amorphous structure, supporting the premise that ultra-rapid cooling suppresses crystallization, but it provides no evidence for the effects of an isothermal hold near Tg, structural relaxation, or the specific crystallization onset temperature (~960 K). E2 discusses computational prediction of glass-forming compositions and critical cooling rates in other alloy systems, offering no direct support for any of the key premises regarding this alloy's behavior under modulated cooling.
premises: Ultra-rapid cooling (>10^5 K/s) can kinetically suppress crystallization in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20
A brief isothermal hold near Tg can induce structural relaxation without nucleation
Structural relaxation reduces internal stresses and the driving force for crystallization
The crystallization onset temperature is ~960 K
Dynamic cooling modulation can be practically implemented during melt-spinning
